decks.domain: Learner permit exam, accommodations and supervised driving

cards.front: What is the rule for use the issuer website?
cards.back: The RMV directs applicants to use its own website because similar third-party sites may add fees or put personal and financial information at risk.

cards.front: What is the rule for permit minimum age?
cards.back: A Class D learner-permit applicant must be at least sixteen.

cards.front: What is the rule for permit exam subject?
cards.back: The learner-permit exam tests Massachusetts motor-vehicle laws and safe-driving practices.

cards.front: What is the rule for supervised practice?
cards.back: A learner permit permits practice driving with a licensed operator who is at least twenty-one.

cards.front: What is the rule for permit duration?
cards.back: A learner permit can remain valid for up to two years.

cards.front: What is the rule for prepay license fees?
cards.back: Road-test and license fees may be prepaid when applying for the learner permit.

cards.front: What is the rule for paid fees and license delivery?
cards.back: When the required fees have been paid, the license is sent automatically after a successful road test without another RMV Service Center visit.

cards.front: What is the rule for application visit?
cards.back: An applicant submits the learner-permit application during a reserved RMV Service Center visit and may prepare the application online beforehand.

cards.front: What is the rule for minor application signature?
cards.back: A learner-permit applicant younger than eighteen must have a parent or guardian sign the application.

cards.front: What is the rule for driving related health disclosure?
cards.back: The application requires disclosure of conditions or medications that could affect the applicant’s ability to drive.

cards.front: What is the rule for permit exam fee?
cards.back: The learner-permit exam fee is thirty dollars.

cards.front: What is the rule for electronic image and signature?
cards.back: The RMV electronically captures the permit applicant’s photograph and signature.

cards.front: What is the rule for vision requirement?
cards.back: A permit applicant must pass the service-center vision test or submit an RMV vision-screening certificate from a medical practitioner.

decks.domain: Learner permit exam, accommodations and supervised driving

cards.front: What is the rule for exam location options?
cards.back: After submitting the application, an applicant can take the learner-permit exam at the service center or online.

cards.front: What is the rule for permit printing assistance?
cards.back: An applicant who passes online but cannot print the learner permit may ask the RMV to print and mail it.

cards.front: What is the rule for permit is conditional authority?
cards.back: The learner permit grants conditional driving privileges and is not intended as travel identification.

cards.front: What is the rule for tested topics?
cards.back: Learner-permit exam topics include alcohol misuse, suspensions, Junior Operator violations, road rules and road-sign identification.

cards.front: What is the rule for testing stations?
cards.back: Automated testing stations at full-service centers display permit-exam questions on video-screen kiosks.

cards.front: What is the rule for closed reference exam?
cards.back: Driver manuals and other reference materials are prohibited during the learner-permit exam and in the testing area.

cards.front: What is the rule for no exam electronics?
cards.back: Wearing or using an electronic device during the learner-permit exam is prohibited regardless of the device’s purpose.

cards.front: What is the rule for audio exam exception?
cards.back: Headphones and other audio devices may be worn during the permit exam only when being used for an audio exam.

cards.front: What is the rule for exam headwear exception?
cards.back: A hat may be worn during the permit exam only for a medical or religious reason.

cards.front: What is the rule for prohibited assistance?
cards.back: Using a manual, other reference or electronic device during the permit exam counts as cheating.

cards.front: What is the rule for cheating investigation?
cards.back: Being caught cheating or attempting to cheat causes an exam failure and further investigation.

cards.front: What is the rule for cheating disqualification?
cards.back: A person found responsible for exam cheating cannot hold any driver license or permit for sixty days.

decks.domain: Learner permit exam, accommodations and supervised driving

cards.front: What is the rule for language request?
cards.back: An applicant whose primary language is not English may request a learner-permit exam in a foreign language.

cards.front: What is the rule for listed language options?
cards.back: The listed Class D exam languages include Arabic, Albanian, Armenian, Burmese, Cambodian Khmer and Cape Verdean Creole.

cards.front: What is the rule for listed language options?
cards.back: The listed Class D exam languages include traditional Chinese, simplified Chinese, Farsi, French, German and Greek.

cards.front: What is the rule for listed language options?
cards.back: The listed Class D exam languages include Hindi, Gujarati, Haitian Creole, Hungarian, Italian and Japanese.

cards.front: What is the rule for listed language options?
cards.back: The listed Class D exam languages include Korean, Kiswahili, Laotian, Nepali, Pashto and Polish.

cards.front: What is the rule for listed language options?
cards.back: The listed Class D exam languages include Russian, Brazilian Portuguese, Serbo-Croatian in Latin script, Somali, Spanish and Tagalog Filipino.

cards.front: What is the rule for listed language options?
cards.back: The listed Class D exam languages include Turkish, Thai, Ukrainian, Urdu, Vietnamese and American Sign Language.

cards.front: What is the rule for audio exam operation?
cards.back: Audio exams are offered both at automated testing stations and online, with a voice reading questions and possible answers through headphones.

cards.front: What is the rule for audio language options?
cards.back: Class D audio exams are available in the languages listed for the Class D exam.

cards.front: What is the rule for audio access?
cards.back: Anyone may choose an audio exam without scheduling it in advance or providing extra eligibility documents.

cards.front: What is the rule for bring headphones?
cards.back: An applicant wanting audio at an RMV Service Center should bring headphones to connect to the automated station’s universal headphone splitter.

cards.front: What is the rule for accommodation eligibility?
cards.back: A cognitive or physical disability that prevents a standard exam may support a request for a reasonable testing accommodation.

cards.front: What is the rule for possible accommodations?
cards.back: Possible testing accommodations include additional time or a designated RMV employee reading the exam aloud.

cards.front: What is the rule for request information?
cards.back: An accommodation request should include the applicant’s name, telephone number, requested accommodation and preferred service center.

cards.front: What is the rule for supporting documentation?
cards.back: The RMV may require disability-related documentation suited to the condition and the testing accommodation requested.

cards.front: What is the rule for approval notification?
cards.back: The RMV informs the applicant whether the testing-accommodation request has been approved.

cards.front: What is the rule for ASL request?
cards.back: To request an American Sign Language interpreter, an applicant gives the RMV their name, telephone number and preferred service center, after which the RMV contacts them to schedule the exam and request the interpreter.

decks.domain: Learner permit exam, accommodations and supervised driving

cards.front: What is the rule for carry the permit?
cards.back: A learner must carry the permit whenever driving until a Junior Operator License or full license is earned.

cards.front: What is the rule for qualified supervising driver?
cards.back: A Class D permit driver must have a licensed operator in the adjacent passenger seat who is at least twenty-one, has a valid Massachusetts or other-state license and has at least one year of driving experience.

cards.front: What is the rule for permit nighttime exception?
cards.back: Between midnight and five in the morning, a permit driver younger than eighteen must have a parent or legal guardian along who holds a valid operator license and has at least a year of experience driving.

cards.front: What is the rule for other state permit driving?
cards.back: A Massachusetts Class D permit may be used to drive in another state only when that state’s laws allow it.

decks.domain: Learner permit exam, accommodations and supervised driving

cards.front: What is the rule for minor driver education?
cards.back: Drivers younger than eighteen must take professional driving lessons through a high school or driving school.

cards.front: What is the rule for licensed driving school?
cards.back: Every Massachusetts professional driving school, including a public or private high-school program, must be licensed and monitored by the RMV.

cards.front: What is the rule for verify the school license?
cards.back: An applicant uncertain about a driving school’s credentials can ask to see its RMV license certificate.

cards.front: What is the rule for junior education certificate?
cards.back: An applicant from sixteen and a half to eighteen must complete an approved driver-education program and final exam and have the certificate electronically filed with the RMV.

cards.front: What is the rule for supervised practice requirement?
cards.back: The supervised-driving requirement is forty hours, or thirty hours after completion of a driver skills development program.

cards.front: What is the rule for parent education participation?
cards.back: A parent or guardian must attend two hours of the driver-education curriculum unless they attended during the previous five years.

cards.front: What is the rule for correct class permit?
cards.back: A learner permit of the correct class is required before a road test can be scheduled.

cards.front: What is the rule for road test attempt limit?
cards.back: A Class D applicant may attempt no more than six road tests during a twelve-month period.

cards.front: What is the rule for advance cancellation?
cards.back: Canceling or rescheduling a road test with more than seventy-two hours of notice carries no additional fee.

cards.front: What is the rule for certified instructor sponsor?
cards.back: A driving instructor may sponsor a road test only when the instructor’s school is RMV-certified.

cards.front: What is the rule for retest waiting period?
cards.back: After a road-test failure or a missed appointment, an applicant must wait at least fourteen days before another road test.

cards.front: What is the rule for late arrival consequence?
cards.back: An applicant who arrives late for the road test will not be tested and must pay the road-test fee.

cards.front: What is the rule for pay fees before scheduling?
cards.back: All outstanding fees must be paid before a new road test is scheduled.
